terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Copy and move what the jobs ask for, then list both places to see the result.

tasks.title: File the loose invoice
tasks.description:
`invoice-0303.csv` is loose in the top folder. Move it into `invoices/march`, keeping its name.

Check looks for `invoices/march/invoice-0303.csv` with the invoice's contents, and checks that it is no longer in the top folder.
nextSteps: List the top folder and `invoices/march` to see where things are now.
Move the invoice with the command from the lesson, naming the folder as the place it goes.
List both places again: the invoice should be in one of them only.
hints: Copying would leave the invoice in the top folder as well. The lesson has a command that takes it away from where it was.
`mv` takes what to move first and where it goes last. A folder as the last name keeps the file's name.
From the top folder, run `mv invoice-0303.csv invoices/march`.

tasks.title: Give the fox poster a proper name
tasks.description:
The fox poster in `artwork` is called `fox-poster-FINAL-v2-REAL.svg`. Rename it to `fox-poster.svg`, in the same folder.

Check looks for `artwork/fox-poster.svg` with the poster's contents, and checks that no file is left under the old name.
nextSteps: Run `ls artwork` to see the long name. Tab can type it for you.
Rename it with the same command you use to move.
Run `ls artwork` again to see only the new name.
hints: Renaming is moving a file to a new name in the same folder.
`mv` with the old name first and the new name last renames. Both are paths, so both start with `artwork/` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Keep a copy of the old prices
tasks.description:
Hesper is about to change `prices.csv`. First make a copy of it called `prices-2025.csv` in the top folder. `prices.csv` stays where it is, unchanged.

Check compares both files with the price list the issue started with.
nextSteps: Make the copy with the command from the lesson, giving the new name as the second name.
Run `ls` and find both names in the top folder.
If `prices.csv` went missing, you moved it instead: put it back first.
hints: A copy leaves the original where it was. The lesson's command for that is two letters.
`cp` takes the file to copy first, then the name of the copy.

tasks.title: Back up the orders folder
tasks.description:
Idris wants a backup of the whole `orders` folder before sorting it: a folder called `orders-backup` in the top folder, holding a copy of everything in `orders`, the month folders and their orders included.

Check compares every file in `orders`, as the issue started, with the one at the same place in `orders-backup`, and checks that `orders` is still there as it was.
nextSteps: Look at what `orders` holds, with its subfolders: `ls orders` and `ls orders/2026`.
Copy the whole folder in one command, to the new name `orders-backup`.
List `orders-backup` and `orders-backup/2026` to see the copy.
hints: `cp` on its own refuses a folder. The lesson names the option that copies a folder with everything inside it.
`cp -r` copies a folder and all it holds. Name the copy as the second name, while `orders-backup` does not exist yet.
Run `cp -r orders orders-backup` from the top folder.
